problems.problem: The reading does not parse: ‘takes the ‘evil beasts’ as ceasing to harm, the land, while the commandments are kept, being as the world was before Adam’s sin’ strands ‘the land’ between commas, so the reader cannot tell that Ramban’s reason (the land, while the commandments are kept, is as the world before the first man’s sin) grounds the beasts ceasing to harm.
problems.fix: Among the blessings for keeping the statutes comes safety in the land; Ramban, on 26:6, takes the ‘evil beasts’ as ceasing to harm, since while the commandments are kept the land will be as the world was before Adam’s sin, when no beast killed a man. (43 words; same evidence, Ramban on 26:6)

problems.problem: The two-commentator form breaks: Rashi ‘hears Moses telling Aaron …’ has no ‘as’, so the elided ‘and Rashbam, on 10:3, as a charge’ has nothing to attach to and reads as if Moses were the charge; ‘now sees the sons as greater’ also drops what they are greater than (Rashi: than me and than you).
problems.fix: When fire from the LORD consumes Nadab and Abihu after their strange fire, Moses speaks to their father; Rashi, on 10:3, hears Moses saying he had expected the sanctuary to be hallowed through himself or Aaron and now sees the sons as greater than both, and Rashbam, on 10:3, a charge not to mourn or leave the service. (56 words; same evidence)

problems.problem: The context clause leaves the day’s passage: Moses asking for a shepherd is Numbers 27:15 to 17, which is day 52’s reading, and it is not even what immediately precedes (Joshua’s commissioning, 27:18 to 23), so the clause is both outside the passage and inexact; the sequence it implies is the link Rashi and Numbers Rabbah 21:2 draw, not the text’s own.
problems.fix: Opening a calendar of offerings for day, sabbath, new moon and feast, the LORD charges Moses; the Midrash, Numbers Rabbah 21:16, reads ‘My food’ as spoken by One who needs no offerings, the whole world being His and every beast offered His creation. (42 words; reading unchanged)

problems.problem: The key verse prints a visible defect at the head of the day: ‘fathers’houses’ with no space (the app’s JPS text loses the space after this apostrophe throughout Numbers 1 to 2, a transcription fault, not the 1917 translation), and it opens on a quotation mark that never closes within the verse. Rule 8 forbids repairing it in the key, so the entry shows a typo as scripture.
problems.fix: Either have the operator repair the systematic missing space in the app’s text (fathers’ houses) and rerun verse.js on the same key, or ship the standby tanakh-02-d042-s (Numbers 2:17, Sforno) once verified; the Rashi and Ibn Ezra reading on 2:2 is sound and can stand unchanged if the text is repaired.

problems.problem: The image is left without its point: ‘the true king being whoever is free of the desires’ hangs as an absolute clause after the derivation, so the reader is not told that Ibn Ezra himself says this (his own ‘ודע’) nor how it bears on the crowned Nazirite.
problems.fix: After wine and the razor, the Nazirite law turns to the dead; Ibn Ezra, on 6:7, takes as not far-fetched the view that the Nazirite is named from the crown on his head, and calls whoever is free of the world’s desires the true king. (43 words; same evidence, his ‘תאוות העולם’)
